caption_used: Distribution of samples (%) across varying values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (outer ring) and sample-level maximum ambiguity (inner ring). The outer ring shows that nearly half of all samples (49.0%) exhibit zero ambiguity standard deviation (Std: 0.0), followed by Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, with the remaining samples distributed between Std: 0.82 at 7.0% and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. In the inner ring, Max Ambiguity of 1 accounts for approximately 39.0% of samples, Max: 2 represents the largest inner-ring segment at 47.7%, and Max: 3 comprises 14.2%. The two rings together indicate that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures.
raw_response: The chart is a donut chart with two concentric rings representing two different levels of ambiguity. The outer ring, labeled "Ambiguity Std (Outer)," shows the distribution of samples across different values of sample-level ambiguity standard deviation (Std). The inner ring, labeled "Max Ambiguity (Inner)," shows the distribution of samples across different values of sample-level maximum ambiguity (Max). The outer ring has four segments with the following percentages: Std: 0.0 at 49.0%, Std: 0.47 at 38.0%, Std: 0.82 at 7.0%, and Std: 0.94 at 5.0%. The inner ring has three segments with the following percentages: Max: 1 at 39.0%, Max: 2 at 47.7%, and Max: 3 at 14.2%. The chart indicates that the majority of samples exhibit low ambiguity across both measures, with the highest percentage of samples having a Max Ambiguity of 1.
